html:
The Newe, or Western Shoshone, are a people of the Great Basin, the dry country of central and eastern Nevada and nearby California. They speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, like the Northern Paiute, Southern Paiute and Goshute.

In a land of little water they lived in small family groups that moved through the year. They gathered pine nuts in autumn, collected seeds and roots, and hunted rabbits and pronghorn in communal drives.

Settlers and miners on the routes to California crossed their land from the 1840s. In the Treaty of Ruby Valley of 1863 they allowed roads, mines and ranches but did not sell their land. The United States later treated most of it as public land, and in the 1950s nuclear tests began at a site on territory the Newe still claim. They refused the money the government offered in 1979 in place of the land, and the dispute is still open.
